problem: Ogg assembly ignores a fresh-page flag while a known packet is unfinished,and treats an initial continued fragment with unavailable prefix as a full codec packet. Packet-looking bytes in legal decoder padding expose wrong10/30/40ms clocks.

references.finding: Joined live streams can begin audio with a continued fragment. A fragment without its preceding pieces must not be decoded. Fresh flags while previous packet continues also prohibit decoding that packet.
Decoders must accept arbitrary padding bytes,though conforming encoders emit zero padding. Decoder-acceptance test padding can therefore contain packet-shaped bytes.

requirements: All pages have valid CRCs and consecutive counters,so FVID0170 counter rejection cannot substitute for this fix.
Validate missing flags specifically;distinguish an existing codec refusal on zero-byte false packets from successful playback acceptance.
Discard joined fragments until a genuine packet begins. Do not blanket-refuse initial continuation,which is a defined RFC7845 live-join case.
Eight complete/prefix controls retain exact codec bytes and native PCM/worker seek/EOF,including nil termination and empty-page compatibility.

The standalone reader already refuses malformed flags and currently refuses joined prefixes as unsupported. Preserve refusals and enable its joined-prefix acceptance with the implementation,including rewind.
All fixture generation remains pure/offline and explicit;ordinary tests do not depend on libopus,FFmpeg or network.
counting: Plan one continuation-aware packet-state improvement,not separate IDs per flag direction,partial-page layout,reader or sample clock.

supplementary_before.result: The sequence-aware actual frozen parser publishes the exact wrong fragment bytes in all six malformed/joined cases while eight complete controls remain intact. This is parser proof;native clocks/worker and standalone acceptance gates remain required.

implementation_plan: Represent a known packet prefix separately from a continuation whose prefix is unavailable. Publish only complete known packets.
A fresh nonempty page while a known packet is unfinished must refuse specifically;do not decode packet-shaped bytes from that tail.

A valid joined initial continuation is not a blanket error:discard all of its segments until its terminating lace,then retain whole packets and original granules. Nil termination and multi-page fragments matter.

Keep generic empty-page compatibility without inventing packet boundaries from an empty segment table. The specialized streaming reader currently explicitly refuses empty segment tables;do not silently present that as playback acceptance.

The standalone reader needs an explicit headers/first-audio/discarding/regular phase. Rewind must restore first-audio fragment handling as well as FVID0170 counter checkpoint. Preserve malformed-flag refusal and packet-buffer bounds.

Native healthy/joined playback must match independent raw-packet PCM and actual mid-packet/EOF worker traces. The before30/40ms joined and10ms malformed clock hypotheses still require Cargo/runtime proof.
One cohesive continuation-state improvement,not separate IDs per state,reader,profile or fixture.

implementation: Canonical pending state distinguishes available prefix from missing prefix;missing fragments never count against published packets and discard through terminating lace. Empty pages preserve pending state. Fresh nonempty pages cannot bypass a known unfinished packet.

Streaming reader distinguishes header,first-audio,discarding and regular phases. Discard-only pages advance page counters and retain only page-local payload,then whole packet publication resumes. Rewind restores first-audio phase alongside the sequence checkpoint.
No public interface,codec synthesis,buffer limit or claimed performance change.
